narrative.intro: Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy obligated $232M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy received 3 awards so far, with an average award size of $77.3M. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy obligations are down 22.6% year over year. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy obligations by fiscal year show variability: $120M in FY21, $274M in FY22, $196M in FY23, $244M in FY24, $299M in FY25, and $232M in FY26. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy concentrates work in a few NAICS markets. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy top markets in FY2026 to date are Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences at $134M, Optical Instrument and Lens Manufacturing at $71.4M, and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) at $26.2M. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy current-year totals are fiscal year to date and the figures above reflect contract obligations unless otherwise noted.

sections.heading: How has Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy's contracting trended year to year?
sections.body: Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy obligations rose from $120M in FY21 to $274M in FY22, then fell to $196M in FY23 before climbing to $244M in FY24 and $299M in FY25, and then decreased to $232M in FY26. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy obligations are down 22.6% year over year in the current fiscal-year-to-date period.

sections.heading: What markets does Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy serve this year?
sections.body: Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy leads in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences with $134M in obligations in FY2026 to date. Association of Universities for Research In Astronomy also records $71.4M in Optical Instrument and Lens Manufacturing and $26.2M in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology).
